purpose: Paper replication failures that have been investigated and are kept as failures. Each is bound to its case definition, frozen target and tolerance, and the value it fails with; the audit accepts it only while the observed value stays within the regression bound. Targets are never changed here.
regression_basis: The engine is deterministic for a given image; the observed values were reproduced bit for bit across runs.

failures.finding: FEMM's 2D phase inductance with the stated magnet permeability 1.22 is 3.5% above the paper's 2D FEA value. With unit magnet permeability it is 1.1607 mH, within 0.06%; the paper's 14 mm effective air gap (magnet depth plus gap) also implies unit permeability, so the paper's FEA most likely treated the magnets as air.

Where stator and rotor poles overlap, FEMM's phase flux linkage exceeds the paper's FEM curves (Fig. 8) by a factor that depends on rotor position but not on current: the paper's values are 0.973, 0.967 and 0.961 times the model's at 15, 20 and 30 degrees from 2 to 18 A, while unaligned and at 10 degrees they agree within 0.0003 and 0.0043 Wb. The mesh is converged and each input varied alone (geometry, coil, steel, gap, turns) changes the curves' shape rather than scaling them; Fig. 13 at native resolution confirms the pole widths within 1%. Likely cause, found by diagnostics outside the case: an unstated lamination stacking factor in the authors' steel with a small gap-like term. FEMM's lamination fill 0.96 removes the excess above 10 A at every position, and with a 0.415 mm gap (or rotor faces in 3.6 degree chords) the paper's 44 readings are matched with 0.24% rms (0.21%), against 2.65% for the frozen model; Fig. 10's torques, not fitted, come within 1.1-2.7%. These are inputs the paper does not state, not a measurement procedure, so the case keeps its frozen inputs.
related: controls mesh-0p6, table-bore-reading, rotor-root-from-height, parallel-rotor-poles, coil-blocks-diagonal-reading, steel-hot-rolled, air-gap-0p42

failures.finding: Every phase voltage per turn is the table's value times 1.4135-1.4138 (sqrt 2 = 1.4142): the model's voltage assessor reports the peak magnitude of the phasor, and Tables I and III give rms voltages. The torques and losses fix the current as 310 A/cm^2 rms; with 310 A/cm^2 read as the amplitude (control current-density-amplitude-310) every voltage agrees within 0.05% but every torque and loss is halved. The frozen voltage targets compare a peak with an rms value; they stay as frozen.

Two of 24 flux-linkage targets miss Motor-CAD's maps (File S5) narrowly: psi_d at no load is 2.86% low (0.00215 Wb against a 0.002 Wb tolerance) and psi_q at (0, 100 A) 1.23% high (0.00204 Wb). The mesh is converged (0.7 times moves each by under 0.15 mWb) and the shaft does not matter. Solid steel worsens both (-3.99% and +4.22%). Magnets at 20 C instead of the frozen 40 C bring both within tolerance but move psi_d at (0, 200 A) from +0.04% to +2.83%, so magnet temperature does not explain the map as a whole. The maps are interpolations between Motor-CAD FE points whose conditions the paper does not state. Inputs stay as frozen.

The initial design and five further designs agree with the analytic stall torques within 1%, but 16/3 is 3.07% low and Table 3's Designs 1, 4 and 5 about 1.3% low and Design 2 2.39% high. The mesh is converged (0.7 times moves the torques by 0.1%), the iron is effectively infinitely permeable (ten times more moves them 0.07%), and the rounding of Table 3's variables moves them by at most 0.3%. 16/3 is also the one combination below the paper's own FEM, and Design 2's stated PM mass is 4% off the others. The causes are open; inputs and targets stay as frozen.

The inner bar's skin factors at 50 Hz, k_ri = 4.81 and k_xi = 0.932, miss the text's 2.36 and 0.955, but those text values belong to the paper's approximate circuit: its Fig. 8 plots the FE skin factors, which read 4.77 and 0.931 at 50 Hz. The case froze the text values as FE skin factors; they stay frozen. The inner bar's DC self-inductance is 1.01% high (6.569 against 6.503 uH/m), with all three inductances 0.6-1.0% high and the mesh converged (halving it moves them under 0.06%); Fig. 1's dimensions are printed to 0.1 mm.

Every torque is 27-36% above the paper's (Table 3 at rated current, Fig. 11 at 2/3 of it) by a nearly uniform factor: the torque-angle curve's shape matches within 1.1% and the factor is the same at both currents; no control moves the torque by more than 3.2%. Fresh look (2026-10-27) with the authors' Energies 2017 paper on the same lamination (ibrahim-2017-ferrite-pmasynrm): the same construction is high there too, by 7.5-16.7% with a gap's signature that a 0.36 mm effective gap removes; with that gap this case's targets still exceed by 9-23%, now tilted with current angle, whereas at the stated 0.30 mm gap they are a flat 1.28-1.32 and this paper's own Fig. 10 inductances follow the 0.30 mm build's shape (Ld 0.93-0.95 of it at every current). So this paper's results are this construction at the stated gap scaled uniformly by about 0.77, as an unstated effective length of 106-109 mm would make them, unlike its sibling's. The stated turns, current, rating and stator are consistent with the 2017 machine (165 against 159 A per slot at the same current density; each rating is its own FE torque times its speed), and this case's readings are confirmed (its FE plot shows the prototype as built here, IoU 0.85; the drawn 2017 stator changes the torque +0.2%). The cause lies in this paper's FE (its measurements agree with it), localized but not identified; inputs and targets stay as frozen.
related: controls rib-0p8, barrier-ends-full-width, steel-m45, shaft-steel, shoe-depth-1p2, current-amplitude-22, mesh-0p7

failures.finding: Example 1 is within 0.64 N m of Fig. 12's FEM points (rms 0.44 N m on a 74 N m curve, fundamental +0.6%), failing five of 13 points at the 1% tolerance. Example 2's fundamental and 3rd harmonic agree with Fig. 17's points (40.46 against 40.39 N m) but its 45th and 51st order ripple is in antiphase with them, so the points alternate between +27.5% and -10.8%. A meshed-gap diagnostic agrees with the sliding band within 0.6% and mesh 0.6 moves results by 0.2%, so the construction is not the cause; the relative angle of the outer magnets and pole pieces, which the paper does not state, could be.

Fig. 19's static torque contradicts Fig. 10 and the stated currents: with phase A's EMF largest at 0 degrees, Ia = I and Ib = Ic = -I/2 give the largest torque there, where Fig. 19 is zero. With the current phasor turned 270 electrical degrees (Ia = 0, Ib = -Ic = -(sqrt 3/2) I) the same model reproduces Fig. 19's 38 FEM points within 0.069 N m rms at the stated peak current; moving the rotor origin instead fits no better than 2.4 N m. No load passes.

Fig. 18's static torque is zero at the sweep's start, which the stated currents and the model's rotor reference do not give (8.8 N m there). An exact scan over current phase for both slot readings (the model is linear) fits Fig. 18 at best within 1.24 N m rms (frozen slots) or 0.91 N m (half-slot reading, -12.5 degrees), against 13.5 and 4.4 at the stated phase; the assumed slot positions move the load torque by up to 97%. The cause is open; the EMF passes.

Every measured target is exceeded by a nearly uniform factor while the shapes match: the line-to-line back-EMF constant is 1.598 V/Hz against 1.338 (+19.4%), and the locked-rotor peaks are 13-18% high from 50 to 250 A, with each model curve correlating with Table 3.2 at 0.998-0.999 (its slot-ripple bumps fall at the measured angles) and fitting it as 1.13-1.18 times the measurement within 2-3% of the peak. The one-pole sector equals a full cross-section (flux 0.002%, torque 0.02-0.1%), and the mesh, the drawing's air gap, M-36 steel, a 0.96 fill, an air shaft and 60 C magnets move the results by 0-5%; a dc test current fed line to line would raise them. The model's low-current inductances (Lq 5.1 mH, Ld 2.05 mH at 50 A) match the report's static 5 and 1.92 mH, while its magnet flux linkage is 19% above the one the measured back-EMF implies (independently confirmed by the thermal report's no-load supply of 80-85 V at 60 Hz with 1.5-3.5 A). A diagnostic with the remanence lowered to 1.05 T matches the back-EMF within 3% and the low-current peaks within 1-5%, but leaves 200-250 A 8-10% high; the whole set behaves as the model scaled by 0.86 (an effective length near 72 mm), which the stated 84 mm stack and the 19.05 kg core mass rule out. Cause open: weaker installed magnets than the hysteresisgraph sample, or 3D magnet-end effects, are the leading candidates.

failures.finding: Two kinds of failure, both investigated. Average torque at 1.0 and 1.6 A: the model gives 0.198 and 0.531 N m against Table 2's FEMM averages 0.22 and 0.55, while its maximum torques (0.302, 0.797) and every plateau point of Fig. 11 agree with the paper; integrating the paper's own Fig. 11 simulated curves over 0-22.5 degrees gives 0.066, 0.198 and 0.531 N m, so Table 2's calculated averages at 1.0 and 1.6 A do not follow from the curves they were computed from (the model matches the curves within 0.3%, and the table's measured averages 0.07/0.20/0.53 as well). Unaligned inductance (AC curve, 0.7 A): 24.10 mH against 23.4 mH derived from the text's rounded 35% (Fig. 9(a) reads 23.75 mH); the model follows Fig. 9(a) within 0.8% from 0 to 16 degrees and the excess grows to 1.5-2.4% only toward unaligned, where leakage through the slots dominates. No control lowers it (mesh +0.2%, steel +0.2%, fill -0.2%, shaft 0%; Table 1's pole arcs raise it 4.6%); cause open, likely undrawn detail of the authors' air regions or mesh.

Every acceptance quantity is 23-28% below the paper's with the frozen magnetization curve (Table 1's five GOST points from 1.54 T, FEMM's origin below them, about 1225 relative permeability): flux per pole 6.80 against 9.063 mWb, psi_m1 0.727 against 0.963 Wb, rated torque 72.9 against 97.72 N m. The model's iron below 1.54 T is far too reluctant: control bh-low-field (a typical lamination's low-field shape below 1.50 T joined to Table 1) raises every value 33-40%, to within 0.4-2.5% of the paper (rated-load psi_m1 +0.43%, equivalent EMF +0.49%, final torque +0.77%; SIM flux and flux linkage +2.3-2.5%, rated torque +2.3%) and reproduces Table 3's harmonics and the 8.09/7.75 A saturation ratio (1.0107 against 1.0099). The author's FEMM curve therefore had a realistic low-field part the paper does not print (likely in the 2023 companion paper). Mesh (0.75: under 0.13%), bridges (under 1.2%), slot widths (under 0.7%), shaft (under 0.9%) and stacking (2%) explain none of it.

Investigated. With the frozen magnet recoil permeability 1.05 the ideal-iron model gives xi_10 = 971.7 N m for the HAL-CMG (+1.96%) and 849.1 N m for the standard CMG (+1.94%), and the standard CMG's xi_4 = 339.0 N m (+1.55%); the HAL-CMG's xi_4 passes at 385.3 N m (+0.90%). The result is numerically settled: mesh 0.75 moves every amplitude by under 0.03%, an inner-rotor sweep (diagnostic) gives the HAL-CMG amplitudes within 0.24%, and meshed linear iron agrees with the unmeshed ideal iron within 0.04% at one position. The magnet permeability, which the paper does not state, decides the outcome: the controls at 1.0 and 1.1 move the amplitudes by +4.4 to +5.3% and -3.9 to -4.1%, and all four would lie within 1.5% for a permeability of about 1.06-1.075. The paper's xi_10/xi_4 is 2.4954 for both drives (to five digits, a constant of its analytic model) while the field gives 2.522 (HAL) and 2.505 (standard), so no single permeability brings both rotors of both drives within 1% of Table 3; the paper's own FEA differs from its analytic values by 1-1.5%.

Investigated. At the frozen current (the FEA winding loss at copper's 20 C resistivity, 2.69 A/mm2 rms) the rated torque is 1155.3 N m against Fig. 14's FE mean 1015.46 (+13.8%), with the stress tensor (1154.5) and the flux-linkage torque (1154.9) agreeing within 0.07%. It is numerically settled (mesh 0.85 and 1.25: within 0.03%), and the winding, d-axis and phase order are confirmed by the phase_linkage assessor (0.001 electrical degrees) and by the current-angle steps (the torque peaks between 90 and 110 degrees). The conductor temperature behind the paper's winding loss decides the outcome: the control with copper at 120 C gives 1016.24 N m (+0.08%), and interpolating the two puts the match at 2.27 A/mm2, copper at about 121 C; at that current the 2D internal power factor is 0.756 against the paper's 0.78, where the frozen current gives 0.698. No other input moves the torque that far: magnets at 1.30 T -5.2%, recoil permeability 1.10 -0.9%, a magnetic hub +1.6%, Table V's stator yoke +0.6%, solid M-43 +0.3%, the literal slot opening +0.03%, copper density 8890 -0.3%; the literal 5 A/mm2 gives 1652.5 N m (+63%). The frozen 20 C reading was argued from the measured winding loss exceeding the FEA's; the result says the FEA used hot copper, a class-F design temperature.

failures.finding: Investigated. At the drawn and tabulated 0.30 mm gap the brain's construction exceeds the paper's Maxwell torque at the optimal current angle for all four prototypes by a current-dependent factor: 1.15-1.17 at half rated current, 1.08-1.10 at Fig. 24's data tips (10.4-10.59 A), 1.07 at rated current, with the optimal angles within 0.6-1.8 degrees, stress-tensor and flux-linkage torque within 0.1%, the text's gains over the S machine reproduced within about 1 point, and every control within 2.1% (mesh 0.7 +0.04%, neighbouring steels +0.3%, solid steel +2.1%, magnetic shaft +0.1%). A likely cause, not a reading: the drawn gap and the frozen magnet stay as they are.
